skill.description: Use AXe CLI to automate iOS Simulator gestures, text entry, hardware buttons, screenshots, video, and accessibility inspection.

content.value_statement: Manual Simulator testing slows UI workflows and accessibility checks. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code repeatable AXe commands for gestures, input, screenshots, video, and inspection.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install AXe CLI with Homebrew.
Lists simulators and stores a UDID for repeatable commands.
Provides tap, touch, swipe, gesture, and hardware button examples.
Covers text input from direct strings, stdin, files, and HID keycodes.
Explains screenshots, video recording, streaming, and ffmpeg piping.
Uses describe-ui for accessibility tree and point inspection.
limitations: Requires macOS with a working iOS Simulator and AXe CLI installed.
Does not automate physical iOS devices.
Command examples may alter the current simulator state.
Screenshots, video, and UI trees can include sensitive app data.

use_cases.title: Run Manual QA Flows Faster
use_cases.description: Use repeatable taps, swipes, text entry, and screenshots to verify app behavior in Simulator.

use_cases.title: Capture Accessibility Evidence
use_cases.description: Inspect accessibility trees and points while collecting visual evidence from the current screen.

use_cases.title: Prototype Simulator Automation
use_cases.description: Turn common UI actions into clear AXe command sequences before creating a fuller test workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Tap a Simulator Element
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for one visible control.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AXe to list simulators, choose the target UDID, tap the button labeled Continue, and report what happened.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Test Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AXe to reach the target screen, capture a screenshot with a clear filename, and summarize any visible issue.

prompt_templates.title: Automate Form Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AXe to fill the email and password fields in the iOS Simulator with test credentials, submit the form, and capture the result.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Repeatable Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an AXe command sequence that waits for the app, scrolls to targetElement, taps it, records video, and inspects the UI tree.

output_examples.input: Tap Continue in the active simulator and confirm the next screen.
output_examples.output: Selected the active simulator, tapped Continue, and verified the next screen by its accessibility label.

output_examples.input: Record a short video while scrolling the product list.
output_examples.output: Started a short simulator recording, performed the scroll gesture, stopped recording, and reported the local video path.

output_examples.input: Inspect the current screen for accessibility labels.
output_examples.output: Collected the screen accessibility tree and summarized missing or unclear labels found in the visible UI.

best_practices: Confirm the target simulator UDID before running commands.
Use test accounts and test data when typing into apps.
Review screenshots, videos, and UI trees before sharing them.
anti_patterns: Do not run commands against an unknown or shared simulator.
Do not type real passwords or private data into test flows.
Do not publish captured media without checking for sensitive content.

faq.question: Does this skill install AXe automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents a Homebrew command. Users should approve installation and review the package source.

faq.question: Can it control real iPhones?
faq.answer: No. The documented commands target iOS Simulator through a simulator UDID.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: You need macOS, iOS Simulator, AXe CLI, and optional ffmpeg for video piping.

faq.question: Can it inspect accessibility labels?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses AXe describe-ui to inspect the screen tree or a specific point.

faq.question: Can it record video?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes AXe recording and streaming examples for simulator sessions.

faq.question: Is captured data private?
faq.answer: Captured data stays local unless shared, but it can include sensitive UI content.
